==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:after|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|after}}, from {{inh|en|ang|æfter}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*aftar}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*after}}, {{m|gem-pro|*aftiri}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₂epo|*h₂epoteros|t=further behind, further away}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₂epo|t=off, away}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|efter|t=after}}, {{cog|frr|efter|t=after, behind}}, {{cog|fy|after}}, {{m|fy|achter}}, {{m|fy|efter|t=behind; after}}, {{cog|nds,nl|achter|t=behind}}, {{cog|de|after-|t=after-}}, {{cog|da,sv|efter|t=after}}, {{cog|nb,nn|etter|t=after}}, {{cog|fo,is|eftir|t=after}}.

The Irish usage to indicate recent completion of an activity is a calque of the Irish collocation {{m|ga|Táim [[tar éis]]...||I have just...|lit=I am after...}}.

** {{audio|en|En-us-after.ogg|a=California}}<!--

* {{hyphenation|en|af|ter}}

===Adverb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L333738}}
{{en-adv|-}}

===Preposition===
{{wikidata lexeme|L3217}}
{{en-head|prep}}

# [[subsequent|Subsequently]] to; [[following]] in [[time]]; [[later]] than.
#: {{ux|en|We had a few beers '''after''' the game.}}
#: {{ux|en|The time is a quarter '''after''' eight.|q=chiefly US}}
#: {{ux|en|The Cold War began shortly '''after''' [[WWII]].}}
#: {{ux|en|'''After''' you with the salt and pepper.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=1|passage=I was about to say that I had known the Celebrity from the time he wore kilts. But I see I will have to amend that, because he was not a celebrity then, nor, indeed, did he achieve fame until some time '''after''' I left New York for the West.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-08|volume=407|issue=8839|page=52|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/international/21579039-chinas-growing-empire-ports-abroad-mainly-about-trade-not-aggression-new-masters The new masters and commanders]|passage=From the ground, Colombo’s port does not look like much. Those entering it are greeted by wire fences, walls dating back to colonial times and security posts. For mariners leaving the port '''after''' lonely nights on the high seas, the delights of the B52 Night Club and Stallion Pub lie a stumble away.}}
## Subsequently to and as a [[result]] of.
##: {{ux|en|Sucess comes '''after''' hard work.}}
## Subsequently to and considering.
##: {{ux|en|I’m not putting you in charge again '''after''' the last disaster.}}
## Subsequently to and [[in spite of]].
##: {{ux|en|'''After''' all that has happened, he is still my friend.}}
##: {{ux|en|I can’t believe that, '''after''' all our advice against gambling, you walked into that casino!}}
## {{lb|en|often with verbs related to cleaning or tidying}} Subsequently to the actions of (someone), in order to remedy a situation.
##: {{ux|en|I'm tired of picking up '''after''' you. Why can't you clean your own messes?}}
## {{lb|en|in reduplicative expressions}} [[repeatedly|Repeatedly]], seemingly in a sequence without end.
##: {{co|en|day '''after''' day, time '''after''' time, mile '''after''' mile, beer '''after''' beer, smile '''after''' smile}}
##* {{RQ:Guardian|title=Is doom scrolling really rotting our brains? The evidence is getting harder to ignore|date=Dec 9 2024|author=Siân Boyle
|text=Paper '''after''' paper spells out how vulnerable we are to internet-induced brain rot.
|url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2024/dec/09/brain-rot-word-of-the-year-reality-internet-cognitive-function
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260226015549/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2024/dec/09/brain-rot-word-of-the-year-reality-internet-cognitive-function}}
## {{lb|en|Irish|Newfoundland|usually|preceded by a form of ''be''|followed by an -ing form of a verb}} {{non-gloss|Used to indicate recent completion of an activity.}}
##: {{ux|en|I was '''after''' finishing my dinner when there was a knock on the door. ''[''{{=}} I had just finished my dinner when ...'']''}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|journal=The Shanachie|title=A Miracle Play|author={{w|Augusta, Lady Gregory|Lady Gregory}}|volume=1|year=1906|passage=Mother: Let him get away out of this now, himself and his share of songs. Look at the way he has your bib destroyed that I '''was after''' washing in the morning!}}
##* {{quote-book|en|title=The Black Box|page=45|author=M. P. Shiel|year=2008|passage="Yes. And where were ''you'' when the flood broke loose?" / "I would be most of the way to the Old House then. O'Loughlin '''was after''' running in wild to tell me he was hearing the Banshee out at The Old House, {{...}}."}}
# [[behind|Behind]].
#: {{ux|en|He will leave a trail of destruction '''after''' him.}}
#: {{ux|en|I told her to shut the door '''after''' her.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''pulled''' the door to after me.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=Then came a maid with hand-bag and shawls, and '''after''' her a tall young lady. She stood for a moment holding her skirt above the grimy steps,{{...}}, and the light of the reflector fell full upon her.}}
# {{senseid|en|pursuing-seeking-etc}} In [[pursuit]] of, [[seeking]]; {{n-g|denoting the [[aim]] or [[object]]}}.
#: {{coi|en|running '''after''' him}};   {{coi|en|what's he '''after'''?}};   {{coi|en|he's '''after''' a job}};   {{coi|en|to thirst '''after''' righteousness}}
#  [[concerning|Concerning]]; in [[relation]] to.
#: {{co|en|to enquire '''after''' a friend; to ask '''after''' her health}}
# In [[allusion]] to, in [[imitation]] of; [[following]] or [[referencing]].
#: {{ux|en|We named him '''after''' his grandfather.}}
#: {{ux|en|This painting is '''after''' Leonardo da Vinci.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1735|title=The Sportsman's Dictionary
|passage=Work your horse in a calade, '''after''' the Italian way; ride him straight, and then you make good use of the calade.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1989|month=May|volume=175|number=5|title=Venezuela's Islands in Time|author=Uwe George|page=549
|text=Angel Falls is named not '''after''' some heavenly being but '''after''' Jimmy Angel, a U.S. bush pilot who came across the falls by accident in 1935 while searching for a gold-rich river he had once visited with a mining engineer.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:Architectural Digest|date=May 2026|volume=83|issue=4|title=Grab a Chair|author=Hannah Martin|page=24
|text=In the 19th century, brothers John and Hugh Finlay pioneered the Baltimore Fancy Chair, modeling its [[klismos]] back not '''after''' firsthand encounters with the ancient Greek perches but '''after''' representations on Grecian urns.}}
# Below, often next below, in [[importance]] or [[rank]].
#: {{ux|en|The princess is next in line to the throne '''after''' the prince.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[according to|According to]] (an author or text).
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} According to the direction and influence of; in proportion to; befitting.
#* {{RQ:Bacon War with Spain|passage=He takes greatness of kingdoms according to bulk and currency, and not '''after''' their intrinsic value.}}

===Conjunction===
{{wikidata lexeme|L333935}}
{{en-head|conj}}

# {{non-gloss|Signifies that the action of the clause it starts takes place before the action of the other clause}}.
#: {{ux|en|The show ends '''after''' the fat lady sings.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''After''' we had decided to call it a day, I went home.}}
#* {{RQ:Birmingham Gossamer|chapter=I|passage=It is never possible to settle down to the ordinary routine of life at sea until the screw begins to revolve. There is an hour or two, '''after''' the passengers have embarked, which is disquieting and fussy.}}
#* '''1991''', Donald "Shadow" Rimgale (character), {{w|Robert DeNiro}} (actor), ''{{w|Backdraft (film)|Backdraft}}''
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May-June|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/david-van-tassel David Van Tassel]; [http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/lee-dehaan Lee DeHaan]|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/wild-plants-to-the-rescue Wild Plants to the Rescue]|volume=101|issue=3|magazine=w:American Scientist|passage=Plant breeding is always a numbers game.{{...}}The wild species we use are rich in genetic variation, […]. In addition, we are looking for rare alleles, so the more plants we try, the better. These rarities may be new mutations, or they can be existing ones that are neutral—or are even selected against—in a wild population. A good example is mutations that disrupt seed dispersal, leaving the seeds on the heads long '''after''' they are ripe.}}

|passage=I did verily believe in my own mind, that I couldn't fight in that way at all; but my '''after''' experience convinced me that this was all a notion.}}

|passage=The amends he had made in '''after''' life were lost sight of in the dramatic glare of the original act.}}

He never read me any of his manuscripts, {{...}} and therefore my lack of detection of his promise may in some degree be pardoned. But he had then none of the oddities and mannerisms which I hold to be inseparable from genius, and which struck my attention in '''after''' days when I came in contact with the Celebrity.}}
# {{senseid|en|nautical}}{{lb|en|nautical|or|aeronautical|where the frame of reference is within the craft}} At or towards the [[stern]] of a ship or the rear of an aircraft.
#: {{ux|en|The '''after''' gun is mounted aft.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''after''' gun is abaft the forward gun.}}
#: {{ux|en|The aircraft provided an '''after''' cabin for two radar operators.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1952|author=C. S. Lewis|title=The Voyage of the Dawn Treader
|passage=Caspian led them down a ladder into the '''after''' hatch.}}

====Usage notes====
* As shown in the examples above, the adverb in this nautical usage is {{m|en|aft}} and the related preposition is {{m|en|abaft}}.
